item.title: Infinite Discs stretches Black Friday into a month-long sale
item.description:
Infinite Discs is doing Black Friday differently this year: instead of a single weekend blowout, the retailer will run sales for the entire month of November. The month will feature new stamp drops, brand spotlights, and deals on discs and accessories, with different brands going on sale at different times.

For disc golfers, the stretched-out format means less pressure to buy everything at once — and more chances to catch a favorite brand's turn. Watch the retailer's schedule through November to time purchases around the brands you throw.

Sources

  • Infinite Discs Blog: A Month-Long Black Friday Sale!

item.title: Zone vs. Zone OS vs. Zone SS: which approach disc to buy
item.description:
The Discraft Zone is one of the most popular approach discs in disc golf, but picking between the original Zone, the Zone OS, and the Zone SS comes down to stability and flight shape. All three are built for approach shots; they differ in how much they fight out of an angle, how much glide they offer, and how aggressively they fade.

The guide's short version: start with the original Zone for most players, grab the Zone OS if you want an extremely overstable disc that holds its line out of almost any angle, and pick the Zone SS for a straighter flight with more glide and a gentler fade.

Sources

  • Foundation Disc Golf - Blog: Which Discraft Zone Should I Buy? | Zone vs Zone OS vs Zone SS Guide

item.title: X-outs, misprints, and factory seconds: how to save money on discs
item.description:
If you've browsed disc golf shops, you've seen discs labeled as X-outs, misprints, or factory seconds — and wondered what you're actually getting. Infinite Discs' guide explains the terminology: X-outs (also called factory seconds) are discs with minor cosmetic or manufacturing imperfections that didn't pass quality control for full-price sale, while misprints carry stamp errors or blemishes.

The key point for buyers: these flaws are almost always cosmetic, not functional, so the disc flies the same for a few dollars less. The guide walks through what each label means and how to search for them, making it a handy primer for anyone looking to stock up or try new molds without paying full price.

Sources

  • Infinite Discs Blog: Disc Golf X-Outs, Misprints and Factory Seconds

item.title: Ricky Wysocki becomes first disc golfer to earn $1 million in career winnings
item.description:
Ricky Wysocki has crossed a milestone no disc golfer has reached before: $1 million in career tournament winnings. The Disc Golf Pro Tour announced the landmark, making Wysocki the first player in the sport's history to hit seven figures in prize money alone.

The figure is a marker of how far professional disc golf has come. A sport that was once a niche pastime now pays its top star at a level that would have been unimaginable a decade ago — and Wysocki, one of the game's defining players, is the one to get there first.

Sources

  • Disc Golf Pro Tour: Ricky Wysocki Becomes First Disc Golfer to Earn $1 Million in Career Winnings
